title: Set a rental snowboard's bindings to a 40 cm duck stance at 15 degrees
instruction: Set this rental snowboard's bindings in a duck stance. Move each binding from its end of the board and set it down flat over a grey insert grid, highback on the board edge nearest you and disc centred on the black centre line, so the two discs are 40 cm apart and centred on the red cross. Turn each binding so its toe end points 15 degrees off straight across the board: the left binding toward the left end, the right one toward the right end. Then let go of both and lift clear.
context: Ski and snowboard rental technicians set every board's stance before it goes out: the stance width from the shop chart for the rider (40 cm here, a child's width on a 110 cm board), centred on the board's reference mark, and the binding angles measured from the board's crosswise line. A common rental default is a duck stance, +15/-15: the front toes turned 15 degrees toward the nose and the back toes 15 degrees toward the tail, so a beginner can ride either way. Each binding sits on the board's centre line so the boot overhangs the toe and heel edges equally; an off-centre binding drags a toe or heel in a turn and catches an edge, a classic beginner fall. The technician checks with a tape and the disc's angle scale (3-degree steps) before screwing down. Done by: counter and rental clerks (O*NET 41-2021.00) and ski and snowboard technicians (classed under 49-9099.00) in resort rental shops.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Four kinds of thing are on the table; all are fixed except the two bindings. (1) Snowboard top: a flat rigid plank of painted plywood or HDPE standing in for a child's board, 1100 mm long along y (y -55 to +55 cm), 240 mm wide (x 18.0 to 42.0 cm) and 10 mm thick, built as three strips with one flush top: white top sheet from x 18.0 to 29.8 cm and from x 30.2 to 42.0 cm, and a black centre line 4 mm wide between them, centred on x 30.0 cm. Its heel edge (x 18.0 cm) faces the robot; its nose is the left end (y +55 cm), its tail the right end (y -55 cm). (2) Reference mark: a red cross of two red vinyl tape strips, each 30 x 4 mm and 0.5 mm thick (the one along y lies on the one along x), crossing at x 30.0 cm, y 0. (3) Insert grids: 16 grey vinyl dot stickers, 8 mm across and 0.5 mm proud of the top sheet (marks, not holes), in two grids of 2 x 4 on a 40 mm pitch at x 28.0 and 32.0 cm: y +14, +18, +22 and +26 cm (nose grid, centred at y +20 cm) and y -14, -18, -22 and -26 cm (tail grid, centred at y -20 cm). (4) Two bindings: identical loose rigid parts of black and grey plastic, 0.25 kg each, made of: a black baseplate 200 mm heel to toe, 120 mm wide and 15 mm thick; a grey disc 90 mm across and 3 mm thick on the baseplate's centre, with a white tick 20 x 4 x 1 mm on it, 22 to 42 mm from its centre toward the toe; a black highback 10 mm thick (heel to toe), 120 mm wide and 80 mm tall standing on the baseplate's heel end; and a grey ankle-strap bar 30 mm (heel to toe) by 130 mm, 37 mm tall, lying across the binding on the disc, centred over the disc's centre, its top 55 mm above the board (the binding's centre of mass is 15 mm from the disc's centre toward the heel and 22 mm up). A binding's centre is its disc's centre, on the baseplate's underside. Its angle is the direction from heel to toe seen from above, in degrees from +x (straight across the board, away from the robot), positive toward the nose. Start: both bindings lie flat on the board's ends with their discs on the centre line (x 30.0 cm): the nose binding's disc at y +44.5 cm, toe toward the nose (angle +90; toe end 5 mm from the nose, highback at y +34.5 to +35.5 cm), and the tail binding's disc at y -44.5 cm, toe toward the tail (angle -90). Nothing else is on the table. The finished stance has the discs at y +20.0 and -20.0 cm on the centre line, angles +15 and -15 degrees, over the insert grids.
scoring: Judged on the end state. A binding is set when all of these hold: it lies flat on the board (its centre, on its underside, within 3 mm of the top sheet's height, and its base tilted 5 degrees or less from level; upside down counts as 180); its disc centre is over an insert grid (14 to 26 cm from the cross along the board, either side: |y| 140 to 260 mm) and within 10 mm of the centre line (x 29.0 to 31.0 cm); its angle is within 3 degrees of its target; it is still (its centre travelled 2 mm or less and it turned 1 degree or less in total over the last 0.5 s); and it is let go, grippers lifted clear: each gripper's axis, from the point midway between its finger tips 38 mm back up, stays 30 mm plus its finger radius or more from every part of the binding (the radius, out to a pad's outer corner: half the finger gap plus 8 mm along the closing direction and 13.5 mm across it; 57 mm fully open, 45 mm at a 70 mm gap, 16 mm closed: 87, 75 or 46 mm in all), so a finger resting on a binding, open or closed, is not let go. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, no binding counts as let go. The binding whose disc is further left (larger y, nearer the nose) is the front binding, target +15 degrees (toe turned toward the nose, the left end); the other is the back binding, target -15 degrees (toe turned toward the tail, the right end). The two bindings are identical, so which one ends where does not matter. A binding turned heel-forward reads about +165 or -165 degrees and is not set. W is the distance along the board (y) between the two disc centres and C the y of their midpoint (0 at the red cross). 1.0: both set, W 390 to 410 mm and C within 10 mm of the cross. 0.75: both set, W 380 to 420 mm and C within 20 mm, but not 1.0. 0.5: both set, W or C outside the 0.75 limits (for example discs at y +24 and -24 cm, W 480 mm; or at +24 and -16 cm, W 400 mm but C 40 mm). 0.25: exactly one set (for example one binding placed and the other left where it lay, even if turned there; or both toes toward the nose, +15 and +15, which sets only the front one). 0: neither set (not moved, or only turned where they lie, which is off the insert grids; off the board or on the other binding; tilted; off the centre line; at the wrong angle, such as both toes turned in, -15 in front and +15 behind; moving; still held or touched, or a gripper not lifted clear). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise the score is the end state at the run limit. In a real trial, once the arms have lifted clear and nothing moves: the strap bar covers each disc's centre, so take the centre midway between the disc rim's heel-most and toe-most points; measure each centre's offset from the centre line and its y from the cross (giving W and C) with a tape; each angle with a protractor against the board's edge (or from an overhead photo); flatness: the baseplate rests on the board, and a 3 mm feeler gauge does not pass under the middle of either long side of it; let go: each gripper's finger tips and the 38 mm above them at those distances from the binding.
fidelity: The board is a flat fixed plank (no camber, sidecut or upturned tips). Each binding is one rigid part at about half a child's binding's weight, with a rigid bar for the ankle strap and no toe strap. The screws into the inserts are not modelled (the insert dots are flat stickers, not holes), so the task ends at the set-up a technician checks before screwing down. One friction for every surface.
reset_notes: Put each binding back on its parked spot on the board's end, toe toward that end and 5 mm from it, disc on the centre line. Nothing is consumed.
